newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open stronger on durable goods data.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open stronger on durable goods data.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger on Thursday, buoyed by weaker than expected U.S. economic data, overseas buying and some short-covering, dealers said.
"Very clearly this morning it was the durable goods orders," said one Toronto-based T-bill trader. "There was some Canadian numbers too, but it was mostly the U.S."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.69 percent from 3.72 percent at Wednesday's close.
Dealers said a rally in bonds, which followed the release of the data, also helped lower T-bill yields.
Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets rallied after the U.S. Commerce department reported that August durable goods fell by a greater-than-expected 3.1 percent.
"I think what you've got primarily is short-covering going on in the cash bills which is dragging down the WI's (when-issueds) with it," said another trader.

Dealers also cited some overseas buying as boosting prices. In other prices, the six-month when-issued bill firmed to yield 4.09 percent from 4.13 percent at Wednesday's close. The one-year when-issued bill firmed to yield 4.36 percent from 4.38 percent.
Dealers said the call loan or overnight lending rate was trading at 4.15-4.20 percent, the top of the Bank of Canada's 3.75-4.25 percent target range.
